steps.title: The endocrine system
steps.body: A system of glands that secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream. Hormones are chemical messengers that travel in the blood to target organs where they produce an effect.

steps.title: Negative feedback
steps.body: A mechanism that maintains stable conditions (homeostasis). When a level rises above normal, the body responds to bring it back down. When a level falls below normal, the body responds to bring it back up. This keeps conditions within a narrow range.

steps.title: How negative feedback works
steps.body: A change from the normal level is detected The body responds to reverse the change The response reduces or counteracts the original change When the level returns to normal, the corrective mechanism is switched off

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Learn the six key glands and their hormones — this is a common recall question The pituitary gland is the "master gland" — it controls many other glands Insulin and glucagon have OPPOSITE effects — insulin lowers glucose, glucagon raises glucose Both insulin and glucagon are produced by the PANCREAS The LIVER is where glucose ↔ glycogen conversion happens (not the pancreas) Type 1 = no insulin production; Type 2 = insulin resistance — don't confuse these When explaining negative feedback, always describe what happens when the level is too high AND too low Negative feedback REVERSES the change — remember this key idea
